why: Dependency ordering. One available report DECLARES a prerequisite, so per the Graypaper it must take the queue path (W^Q) and accumulate after the dependency-free report — even though its prerequisite is already satisfied. Operand order changes what the service computes, so getting this wrong breaks the state root.
family_explainer: The storage family runs a real service that stress-tests service storage. Each block: (1) new work reports are guaranteed onto cores, (2) validators assure availability of earlier reports, (3) once a report has a super-majority of assurances it becomes available and the service's ACCUMULATE entry point executes in the PVM — reading, writing and deleting storage keys via host calls, metered by gas. The post-state root certifies every byte: storage entries, the service's octet/item footprint, gas statistics, the accumulated-set ring and the ready queue.
events: Core 0: package 97417215… guaranteed (5 work item(s), bundle 3555 bytes). It now waits on this core for availability assurances.
6 validator assurance(s): core 0 has 5, core 1 has 6 vote(s). A report becomes AVAILABLE when votes exceed 2/3 of 6 validators (i.e. ≥ 5).

ACCUMULATION: package(s) 51beee85…, 899bce03… became available and were accumulated — the service's accumulate entry point ran inside the PVM. The accumulated-set ring C(15) records them (sorted, ring 11), aging out after 12 blocks.
Service 0 statistics: 9 work item(s) accumulated for 763,763 gas (exact PVM metering — every instruction costs 1, host calls cost 10, log costs 10).
